name: Uganda
summary: A British protectorate around the old Kingdom of Buganda, independent in 1962; Idi Amin’s rule (1971–79) was brutal; Yoweri Museveni has ruled since 1986.

knownFor.label: Source of the Nile
knownFor.note: The White Nile leaves Lake Victoria at Jinja.

knownFor.label: Kasubi Tombs
knownFor.note: Tombs of the kings of Buganda.

location.value: A landlocked country in East Africa, in the African Great Lakes region.

terrain.value: Volcanic hills, mountains and lakes, including part of Lake Victoria; the country lies in the Nile basin.

climate.value: Warm and tropical, with average temperatures of 25–29 °C.

resources.value: Fertile farmland, coffee, fish and largely untapped oil and natural gas.

disasters.value: Landslides in the hills and droughts in the north.

urbanisation.value: Kampala, the capital and largest city, has 1.8 million people.

disease.value: HIV infection has been reduced; there have been several Ebola outbreaks since the first in 2000.

migration.value: In 1972 Idi Amin expelled Ugandan Asians, mostly of Indian origin, cutting about 80,000 Indians to as few as 7,000.

economicBase.value: Services (52% of GDP in 2007) have overtaken farming; coffee is the leading export.

tradeRoutes.value: Traditionally depends on Kenya for access to the Indian Ocean port of Mombasa.

wealth.value: One of the poorest nations in the world.

inequality.value: Large gaps between the capital and rural areas.

governmentType.value: A presidential republic: the president is both head of state and head of government.

keyRulers.value: Milton Obote. Idi Amin. Later and present leaders are not named here.

succession.value: Coups and wars changed leaders until a new leader took power in 1986; presidential term limits were later abolished.

institutions.value: The Parliament of Uganda, with 557 members.

stability.value: Idi Amin's brutal dictatorship (1971–1979), a six-year guerrilla war ending in 1986, and a long struggle against the Lord's Resistance Army.

eliteConflict.value: A nineteen-year ban on multi-party politics was ended by referendum in 2005.

armyAndTech.value: The Uganda People's Defence Forces, which also have representatives in Parliament.

majorWars.value: The Uganda–Tanzania War, which ended Amin's rule in 1979; also involvement in the Congo Wars.

territoryChange.value: The borders drawn by Britain have remained the same since independence.

inventions.value: No major inventions are associated with the modern state.

openness.value: Open to trade and foreign investment, with periods of restriction.

communicationTransport.value: Roads link Kampala to the main towns, and a railway runs to Kenya; Lake Victoria is used for shipping.

religion.value: Mostly Christian: the Catholic Church (39.3%) and the Anglican Church of Uganda (32%) are the largest.

artsArchitecture.value: Bark cloth, a UNESCO-listed craft of the Baganda, and the royal Kasubi Tombs.

socialStructure.value: Many peoples, including the Baganda, whose Buganda kingdom still has a king (Kabaka).

sharedIdentity.value: A national identity shared by many ethnic groups, with English and Swahili as official languages.

dailyLife.value: Many families eat matoke (steamed bananas) and farm small plots.

neighbours.value: Kenya, South Sudan, DR Congo, Rwanda, Tanzania.

riseSignals.value: Independence from the UK on 9 October 1962.

declineSignals.value: None that define the country as a whole.

overallCertainty.value: Basic facts are well documented; some figures are estimates.
